full_independent_source_research.conclusion: WinFsp exposes suitable interception points for implementing a bounded allocated-storage/live-node filesystem. The stock MEMFS example is not the requested global quota/outside-writer boundary. A custom, frozen callback/state/security/cache lifetime contract is required before integration; no current-host support, operational grant or complete issuer follows from this research.

facts: Create checks MaxFileNodes against FileNodeMap count; SetFileSizeInternal checks per-file MaxFileSize before reallocating. No explicit global live allocation reservation ledger is present in these paths.
Cleanup deletes namespace entries, while Close dereferences nodes and deletion frees FileData at final reference release. Rename can remove a replaced target while references survive.

The default root security descriptor grants Everyone full access. Named streams, reparse points, EA/WSL/device-control and optional delayed I/O are example features, not a minimal qualification policy.
LargeHeap allocations round beyond advertised file allocation units; the default funnel initializes the heap without a finite maximum. Node/security/metadata allocations are separate.
Source licensing states GPLv3 or a commercial license; no licensing/provenance choice is made here.
upstream_memfs_observations.inference: Namespace count multiplied by per-file size cannot be treated as a bound on all live objects/backing memory. Deleted-open or replaced nodes must remain charged until actual final release; a heap ceiling alone does not cover every allocation.

concurrency_and_lifetime_contract.facts: Fine guards serialize namespace mutations but permit concurrent I/O on different files. Coarse guards serialize filesystem accesses. Cleanup is not final Close, may precede further operations even for deleted files, and cannot return a failure status.
required_design: One linearizable checked reservation ledger for every live node and rounded allocation, including directories, streams if allowed, pending creates, deleted-open/replaced nodes and asynchronous requests. Reserve before allocation or acceptance; commit once, rollback failures, release only after real final free.

Cover Create, Overwrite, Write/append, SetFileSize, Rename/replacement, delete disposition/Cleanup/Close and all additional allocation APIs. Disable unsupported streams/reparse/EA/WSL/device controls explicitly rather than leave uncharged paths.

Freeze checked arithmetic, allocation rounding, deterministic quota failure, refcount ownership and cancellation/unmount drain. Void Cleanup/Close cannot be the place to retroactively reject an already exceeded cap; internal failure must poison the owner and completion evidence.

cached_and_mapped_io.facts: Fast/cached writes may use the kernel cache. Cached EOF extension first sends SetInformation; paging writes are forwarded with ConstrainedIo and cannot extend EOF. An immediate callback-count policy therefore does not observe every application write or dirty mapped-page event.
cached_and_mapped_io.required_design: A current allocated-capacity quota can reserve all growth before cache acceptance and keep charges through mappings/lazy writes. It is distinct from cumulative bytes written, cache/dirty-page RAM, I/O counts or a universal mapping denial. Specify precisely which resource is bounded, then prove all section/EOF/allocation paths satisfy it or freeze a supported cache/mapping restriction. No such complete proof or configuration was performed.
cached_and_mapped_io.cleanup_fact: The driver retains file-node context until Close to accommodate mapped views and write-behind when files are reopened. Process exit or an empty namespace alone cannot release storage charges or prove filesystem quiescence.

outside_writer_and_confinement.facts: Create/rename requests carry access-token information; Write uses retained file contexts and may be paging I/O. The filesystem's authorization must bind opening contexts rather than assume every later write has the initiating user PID.
outside_writer_and_confinement.required_design: Use a frozen restrictive volume/root security and actual process-identity/confinement contract. A mount name, private directory string, PID list or stock Everyone ACL does not exclude outside writers. AppContainer selective access remains a candidate for restricting child reach; it does not itself demonstrate that unrelated host processes cannot access the mount, or that all Python/backend reads and writes stay inside the intended roots.

next_finite_source_work: Freeze one custom filesystem adapter contract with explicit live-state invariants, every mutation callback, charging/rollback/final-release rules and minimal feature/caching policy; exercise concurrent reservation, delete-open, rename replacement and failure/drain state transitions with synthetic tests only after exact source review.

Integrate that adapter's lifetime/security/resource boundary into the one outer owner and process launcher, including filesystem host/driver identity and failure shutdown. Existing job limits must include all relevant owners; driver/cache memory is not assumed covered by the child job.

Keep native provenance/full resolver/actual host admission and operational setup absent until independently satisfied. Research an exact supported topology before identifying any concrete external fact that requires owner input; no premature input request.
source_receipt_limits: Observed upstream master URLs as web text; no immutable release/version selected and no full-source byte-hash receipt or ABI verification claimed. Exact source/version/license/support pins belong to a future frozen candidate.
Only official repository/header/driver/example/docs and Microsoft AppContainer source documents were consulted. No third-party fork was used as evidence.
